name.text: Classifying stationary points at the origin

questiontext.text:
Each curve below has a stationary point at \(x = 0\). Choose the nature of that stationary point.

\(y = {@c1@}\): [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]
\(y = {@c2@}\): [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]
\(y = {@c3@}\): [[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]] [[feedback:prt3]]
\(y = {@c4@}\): [[input:ans4]] [[validation:ans4]] [[feedback:prt4]]

generalfeedback.text:
If \(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} \gt 0\) at a stationary point it is a minimum point; if \(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} \lt 0\) it is a maximum point. If \(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 0\) the test is silent, not a verdict: test the sign of \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) either side instead.

Curve\(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\)\(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\) at \(x = 0\)Signs of \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) at \(x = -0.1\) and \(x = 0.1\)Nature

\(y = {@c3@}\)\({@d3@}\)\({@v3@}\)[[if test="is(v3=0)"]][[if test="is(gl3>0)"]]\(+\)[[else]]\(-\)[[/if]], [[if test="is(gr3>0)"]]\(+\)[[else]]\(-\)[[/if]][[else]]not needed[[/if]][[if test="is(n3=1)"]]maximum point[[elif test="is(n3=2)"]]minimum point[[else]]point of inflection[[/if]]
\(y = {@c4@}\)\({@d4@}\)\({@v4@}\)[[if test="is(v4=0)"]][[if test="is(gl4>0)"]]\(+\)[[else]]\(-\)[[/if]], [[if test="is(gr4>0)"]]\(+\)[[else]]\(-\)[[/if]][[else]]not needed[[/if]][[if test="is(n4=1)"]]maximum point[[elif test="is(n4=2)"]]minimum point[[else]]point of inflection[[/if]]

A sign pattern \(-, +\) means a minimum point, \(+, -\) a maximum point, and the same sign on both sides a point of inflection.

questiondescription.text:
Differentiation II: classifying stationary points when the second derivative is zero

Grade 12 CBE Core 4.1: Classify the stationary point at the origin of four curves, two of whose second derivatives are zero there.

Core

This question is original to this project.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text:
[[if test="is(kd1=3)"]]

You chose maximum point. At a maximum point the curve rises to the point and falls after it, so the gradient is positive just before it and negative just after. Here \(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 0\) at \(x = 0\), which decides nothing, so work out \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) at \(x = -0.1\) and at \(x = 0.1\) and compare the two signs.

[[else]][[if test="is(kd1=2)"]]

\(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 0\) at \(x = 0\), so the second-derivative test gives no answer, and that does not make the point a point of inflection. Test the gradient either side, for example at \(x = -0.1\) and \(x = 0.1\).

[[else]][[if test="is(n1=1)"]]

You chose minimum point. At a minimum point \(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\) is positive or zero, never negative. Find \(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\) for this curve at \(x = 0\) and look at its sign.

[[else]]

You chose maximum point. At a maximum point \(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\) is negative or zero, never positive. Find \(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\) for this curve at \(x = 0\) and look at its sign.

[[/if]][[/if]][[/if]]
